entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sebastianus, a Western Roman aristocrat and brother to the usurper Jovinus, briefly held the title of Augustus, or co-emperor, in southern Gaul from 412 to 413 CE. His short reign unfolded amidst the tumultuous decline of the Western Roman Empire, a period characterized by widespread political instability, barbarian incursions, and frequent challenges to imperial authority. Sebastianus’s elevation to the purple by his brother was a desperate attempt to consolidate Jovinus’s fragile power base in Gaul and project an image of legitimate dual rule, a common practice in Roman imperial administration, albeit one fraught with peril in this era.

Following Jovinus's usurpation of the Western Roman Imperial throne from Emperor Honorius in 411 CE, largely with the support of Burgundian and Alanic federates, Sebastianus was named Augustus in 412 CE. This act aimed to bolster Jovinus's claim and expand his perceived authority across Gaul, where the central government's control was rapidly eroding. Coins bearing Sebastianus's image were subsequently minted at key Roman centers like Arles and Trier, tangible evidence of his nominal imperial status and the usurpers' efforts to mimic legitimate state functions.

Sebastianus's brief tenure as co-emperor quickly dissolved as the political landscape shifted. The Visigothic king Athaulf, initially an ally of Jovinus, switched his allegiance to Emperor Honorius, perceiving greater advantage in supporting the established authority. This defection proved fatal to the usurpation. Sebastianus was captured and executed in Narbonne in 413 CE, his head sent to Honorius as a trophy, a grim testament to the brutal realities of late Roman imperial politics and the fleeting nature of power outside the recognized imperial line.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Sebastianus's brief tenure as co-emperor highlights the severe political fragmentation and challenges to imperial authority in the Western Roman Empire during the early 5th century, illustrating the desperate attempts of local elites to seize power amidst collapse.
